## All rows (source_id order)
- [S0940] types=[PRINCIPLE, WARNING] scope=OBJECT — "If Model_1 made a bad prediction and a later Model_2 would have predicted correctly, the original decision must not be evaluated using Model_2 -- 'hindsight contamination'. States: evaluate decisions using the knowledge and model available at decision time. Formalizes DecisionBasis(d_t) = K_t + M_t + Policy_t, never K_future + M_future -- 'this allows genuine historical audit'." (anchor: "Avoiding hindsight contamination: evaluate decisions using knowledge/model available at decision time")
- [S0940] types=[DISTINCTION, PRINCIPLE, EXAMPLE] scope=OBJECT — "A reasonable decision given K_t that later fails does not automatically mean DecisionWasWrong -- distinguishes BadDecision from ReasonableDecisionWithUnfortunateOutcome, and Ex ante ('what could reasonably be concluded at decision time') from Ex post ('what do we know after the outcome'), which must remain separate. Decomposes DecisionQuality = f(InformationAvailable, ReasoningQuality, PolicyCompliance, Outcome) -- outcome alone is insufficient. Worked examples: choosing an action with P(Success)=0.9 that then fails does not make the decision irrational (a well-justified decision can suffer a low-probability adverse outcome); conversely an action can succeed despite poor reasoning, so SuccessfulOutcome != GoodDecision -- 'a crucial learning safeguard'. KnowledgeOS should learn from Decision + DecisionBasis + Outcome, not merely Outcome." (anchor: "BadDecision vs ReasonableDecisionWithUnfortunateOutcome; ex ante vs ex post; decision quality != outcome")
- [S0940] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=OBJECT — "Policies evolve Policy_t -> Policy_{t+1}, but old decisions retain PolicyVersion_t, giving DecisionBasis=(K_t,M_t,Policy_t) as 'a complete historical decision snapshot'. Defines DecisionReproducibility: given K_t,M_t,Policy_t,Input_t we should ideally reproduce Decision_t; for a deterministic engine Decision_t=F(K_t,M_t,Policy_t,Input_t), and if identical inputs produce different results the cause (nondeterministic model, changed dependency, hidden state, external service, random seed) must be identifiable and recorded when reproducibility matters." (anchor: "Adaptive governance and decision reproducibility contract")
- [S0940] types=[FORMALIZATION, PRINCIPLE] scope=OBJECT — "For LLM-based reasoning, Decision = F_theta,r(K,M,Policy,Input) where r is randomness/sampling; for auditability KnowledgeOS may need ModelVersion, PromptVersion, ToolVersions, EvidenceSnapshot. But reproducibility does not require deterministic AI: Traceability can be required instead of exact byte-for-byte reproduction -- the system should be able to explain which knowledge, model, policy and evidence were available." (anchor: "Stochastic AI reproducibility: Decision=F_theta,r(...); traceability instead of exact reproduction")
- [S0940] types=[EXTENSION, PRINCIPLE] scope=CROSS-OBJECT — "Proposes a DDD LearningContext boundary responsible for evaluating outcomes, detecting drift, updating models and proposing revisions -- but never silently mutating governance policy or domain facts. A separate GovernanceContext owns Policy; Learning can only propose a PolicyChangeCandidate, since AI/Learning != GovernanceAuthority." (anchor: "LearningContext and GovernanceContext DDD boundaries; AI/Learning != GovernanceAuthority")
- [S0940] types=[EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Runs twelve falsification tests, all PASS: (1) new evidence contradicts an old interpretation => interpretation revised, original evidence unchanged; (2) a model becomes obsolete => historical decisions retain the old model version; (3) a new model performs better => does not automatically replace the active model unless promotion policy allows it; (4) input distribution changes but decision-relevant behavior does not => distribution drift recorded without declaring causal/model failure; (5) statistically significant drift has negligible operational impact => no automatic critical escalation from statistical significance alone; (6) a model predicts poorly despite good historical calibration => performance reevaluated, calibration alone does not protect the model; (7) a successful outcome follows a poor decision => outcome success does not automatically validate decision quality; (8) a justified decision produces an adverse low-probability outcome => not automatically classified as irrational; (9) a governance policy changes => future decisions use the new policy, historical decisions retain the old policy version; (10) a new interpretation of old evidence is created => both historical and current interpretations remain traceable; (11) a model trained on one bounded context detects drift => impact stays scoped to relevant contexts unless evidence supports broader generalization; (12) a candidate model performs well in shadow mode but violates a safety constraint => cannot be promoted." (anchor: "Twelve falsification experiments for Step 45 adaptive-learning model (all PASS)")
- [S0940] types=[RESTATEMENT, PRINCIPLE] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Declares STEP 45 -- PASS and states: Immutable evidence + Versioned interpretation + Governed learning = Safe knowledge evolution; new knowledge may invalidate old conclusions but must not invalidate the historical fact that those conclusions were once justified; Learning != rewriting history; Outcome != proof of decision quality; Drift detection != automatic model invalidation; Model improvement != automatic model promotion; Historical reproducibility requires preserving the knowledge, model, policy, and evidence state used at decision time." (anchor: "Step 45 verdict and six deepest principles of safe knowledge evolution")
